title: Injective augmented Cech resolution on a total simplicial site
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_p$ ($p\ge0$) and $\mathcal D$ be small sites in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $u_\alpha:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_q)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_p)$, for $\alpha:[p]\to[q]$ in the simplex category of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object], be geometric morphisms [def-trf-geometric-morphism] with specified identity and composition isomorphisms satisfying the cocycle laws. Let $a_p:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_p)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ be a compatible augmentation. Form the total topos of families $F_p$ with maps $u_\alpha^{-1}F_p\to F_q$ obeying these coherences, write $r_pF=F_p$, and let $a$ be the geometric morphism whose inverse image sends $G$ to the family $(a_p^{-1}G)_p$. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and use modules over its constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For every injective total module $I$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], the canonical augmented complex
$$0\longrightarrow a_*I\longrightarrow a_{0,*}r_0I\longrightarrow a_{1,*}r_1I\longrightarrow a_{2,*}r_2I\longrightarrow\cdots$$
is exact in every degree and remains exact after applying $\operatorname{Hom}_{\Lambda_{\mathcal D}}(G,-)$ for any module $G$ on $\mathcal D$. Here the $i$-th coface $a_{p,*}I_p\to a_{p+1,*}I_{p+1}$ is $a_{p,*}$ of $I_p\to u_{i,*}u_i^*I_p\to u_{i,*}I_{p+1}$ followed by $a_{p,*}u_{i,*}\simeq a_{p+1,*}$, the differential is their alternating sum, and the augmentation is the component of the counit $a^*a_*I\to I$ transposed under $a_0^*\dashv a_{0,*}$. These maps are natural in $I$.

source.place: Tag 0D7D (lemma-augmentation-cech-complex-modules), with the free-simplex resolution Tag 0D7C (lemma-simplicial-resolution-augmentation-modules); constant coefficients and coherent geometric morphisms use the same family adjunctions.

proof.text: Use [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] for each $u_\alpha$, $a_p$, and $a$: geometric inverse image preserves the constant $\Lambda$ ring sheaf and gives the canonical exact module inverse image, compatibly with composition. To obtain its module Hom adjunction, apply [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-module-transport] with $L=f^{-1}$, $V=f_*$, $R=\Lambda_{\rm target}$, $A=S=\Lambda_{\rm source}$, $eR$ the inverse of the constant-ring comparison, and $c=1$. The required operation comparison is precisely the transported ring comparison of the preceding node. The stated bijection is the restriction of the geometric adjunction to linear maps. Thus all component and total module adjunctions below have the original units and counits and the coherent composite identifications, rather than chosen unrelated adjunctions.

source.place: Tag 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi), module adjunction via finite-product transport; constant coefficient specialization of the ringed setup of 0D7C--0D7D.

proof.text: Fix a module $G$ on $\mathcal D$. The sites, geometric transitions, augmentation coherence and coefficient ring satisfy [lem-trf-total-site-free-module-resolution]. Take its exact augmented complex $P_\bullet(G)\to a^{-1}G$. Its differential sends the $\alpha$ summand to the alternating sum of the $\alpha\delta_i$ summands; its augmentation folds the vertex summands. These are total module maps, with the canonical constant-coefficient lifts fixed in Step 1. Total modules form an abelian category: since each $u_\alpha^*$ is exact by [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image], the componentwise kernels, cokernels and images of a family map inherit transition maps, and the component universal properties give the family ones. Hence exactness of this complex, and the images used in Step 4, are computed componentwise, and injectivity of $I$ refers to this abelian category.

source.place: Tag 0D7C (lemma-simplicial-resolution-augmentation-modules), with its specified face maps.

proof.text:
The module adjunctions of Step 1 and the identity-summand bijection of [lem-trf-total-site-free-module-resolution] identify
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\Lambda_{\mathcal D}}(G,a_{p,*}I_p)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\Lambda_{\mathcal C_p}}(a_p^{-1}G,I_p)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Tot}}(P_p(G),I).$$
For the augmentation degree they identify $\operatorname{Hom}(G,a_*I)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Tot}}(a^{-1}G,I)$. If $f:a_p^{-1}G\to I_p$, precomposing its total extension with $d_i:P_{p+1}(G)\to P_p(G)$ gives at the identity summand $I(\delta_i)\circ u_i^{-1}f$. Its component adjoint is the map on Hom induced by the displayed coface $a_{p,*}I_p\to a_{p+1,*}I_{p+1}$: this follows by substituting the unit formula for the adjoint and cancelling the component unit-counit pair. The augmentation is restriction to component zero, since the fold augmentation corresponds to $1_{a_0^{-1}G}$; the adjoint of the identity $a_*I\to a_*I$ is the counit, so the resulting sheaf arrow is exactly the stated transpose of its zero component. All bijections are natural in $G$ and $I$, and hence identify the whole alternating complexes.

source.place: Tag 0D7D (lemma-augmentation-cech-complex-modules), Hom construction and adjointness, with the explicit face formula in 0D7C.

proof.text: Set $E_p=P_p(G)$ for $p\ge0$, $E_{-1}=a^{-1}G$, and $\partial_0=\epsilon$. Since $I$ is injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions], applying $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Tot}}(-,I)$ to Step 2's exact augmented complex is exact. Explicitly, a cocycle $z:E_p\to I$ kills $\operatorname{im}\partial_{p+1}=\ker\partial_p$, so factors through $\operatorname{im}\partial_p\hookrightarrow E_{p-1}$; the injective extension property extends that factor to $E_{p-1}\to I$. For $p=0$, $\partial_0$ is an epimorphism onto $E_{-1}$ and the factor is the unique preimage in $\operatorname{Hom}(E_{-1},I)$. Precomposition by this epimorphism is injective, giving exactness at the initial augmentation term too. Step 3 therefore proves exactness after $\operatorname{Hom}_{\Lambda_{\mathcal D}}(G,-)$ in all degrees.

source.place: Tag 0D7D, final paragraph: Hom into an injective module is exact, expanded using images and injective extensions.

proof.text: The differentials square to zero because they do so after every Hom test of Step 3: take $G$ to be the source term and apply the composite to its identity. At a term $C^p=a_{p,*}I_p$, take $G=\ker(C^p\to C^{p+1})$. Its inclusion is a Hom cocycle, so Step 4 lifts it to the preceding term (to $a_*I$ when $p=0$). This makes the preceding arrow onto the kernel, proving exactness of the module-sheaf sequence itself. Injectivity of $a_*I\to C^0$ follows from its injectivity under all Hom tests, taking $G$ to be its kernel. Finally a morphism $I\to I'$ postcomposes the Hom complexes and commutes with their natural bijections and the total face and fold maps. Thus it commutes with the stated augmentation and all cofaces, proving naturality in $I$.

source.place: Tag 0D7D, Yoneda construction; explicit kernel test and functoriality.
